correctness.rationale: Taking the trace forces tr(Y)=0 over a field of characteristic two. With diagonal entries of Y both e, off-diagonals f,g, and s=tr(X), the remaining equations are sf=sg=0 and e²+fg+bg+cf=0. If f=g=0 then e=0; otherwise s=0. This gives the two closed pieces as sets. The equation on the trace-zero piece is primitive and linear in c (coefficient f coprime to e²+g(b+f)), hence irreducible; that piece has dimension five and neither piece contains the other. Their intersection fixes Y=0 and s=0, of dimension three. Vanishing of the gradient on the hypersurface forces b=c=e=f=g=0, yielding the singular line of B only. Over F_q, the square root λ of det(Y) is unique. For Y≠0, Y+λI is nonzero rank-one nilpotent, so one can fix Y=λI+E12 and then X has equal diagonals a and lower-left entry λ². Conjugation by uI+vE12 adds tλ² to a and t²λ² to b, where t=v/u. For λ=0 this fixes all q² choices; for λ≠0 it acts freely with unique a=0 representative for each invariant a²+λ²b. The stabilizers have orders q(q−1) and q−1, yielding the two orbit sizes, respectively. The Y=0 stratum gives q²+q ordinary similarity classes by scalar, Jordan, split distinct and irreducible quadratic types, so the three strata sum to 3q², including q=2. Independent field-table matrix tests and stabilizer-weighted counting (python3 /workspace/branches/reproduce_reviews.py 3) reproduced class splits (6,4,2) and (20,16,12), point totals 40 and 1216, nonzero-Y orbit sizes and component point counts for q=2,4. This does not test scheme radicality or prove general geometry; those geometry assertions are expressly reduced.

value.rationale: Counting representations with a chosen basis does not identify isomorphism classes, and the two nonzero-Y strata have different stabilizers. The full characteristic-two orbit classification gives concrete invariants and representatives for all two-dimensional modules over even finite fields, not just the simple ones, and explains exactly how that census differs from the point count. The reduced geometry shows how the characteristic-zero dimension pattern breaks in this example.
